applied.summary: PhaseSpec had no command/argv field, yet the E2E slice runs two `code` phases and DF1.2 INV-1 sourced commandGate argv from 'the DF1.1 manifest (schema-validated at load)' — a `.strict()` schema would have rejected any manifest carrying a command. Added `command?: string[]`, required iff `kind === "code"`, forbidden otherwise; DoD Contract item asserts it.

`retries` was declared in PhaseSpec with no semantics and excluded from the load-time budget invariant, so a retrying run could exceed `callerBudgetMs` by (retries+1)x — the exact ceiling AC5/INV-3 exist to hold. Arithmetic is now `sum((retries + 1) * maxDurationMs) + phases.length * 5000 <= runBudgetMs <= callerBudgetMs`, the bound pinned to `0..5` to match DF1.3 AC1's construction-time rejection, and the boundary test asserts at retries 0 and 1.

Guards/limits was self-negating: it declared P1.6 INV-4's '900s ceiling ... deliberately not reused' and then set the hard upper bound to 900,000 ms (= 900 s). It also misattributed the number — per R2 §3, 600s was P1.6's maxDurationMs bound and 900s was P1.1's `timeoutMs`. INV-3 and AC5 both point at this arithmetic. Rewritten to state the real provenance and keep the 900,000 ms bound without claiming it is not reused.

AC3's echo predicate was written in Python (`text.rstrip(".").casefold()`, `name.replace("_"," ")`) inside a TypeScript story; the literal JS transliteration replaces only the FIRST underscore, so `commit_plan_v2` would escape the check. Restated in TS with `replaceAll`, citing `MOD/data_types.py:49-52` as the source form.
E2E slice's journal record used `manifestVersion` while the owned schema field is `version` — a naming split in the PhaseJournal record shape DF1.4 swaps SQLite behind. Aligned to `version`.

`MOD/` prefixes five Technical Notes citations but expands nowhere in the story (it is `SSSF/templates/adws/adw_modules/`, defined only in R4 §0). Added the R4 §1.1-1.2 anchor and the expansion to Spec Reference, with the D10 read-never-vendored qualifier.

No AC or invariant stated what a failing gate does to phase status. Overview claimed gates are 'the evidence a phase must produce to be allowed to succeed' while AC4 said a failing code block leaves the phase `success`, with nothing distinguishing them — a conformant implementation could report every gate failure and still leave every phase green. Per `MOD/agents.py:163-165` a gate violation raises out of the phase body once the retry budget is exhausted. Added to AC4, to the block-vs-gate Technical Note, and to the unit DoD item; the E2E slice is now explicitly the un-gated block path so it no longer contradicts the new rule.

`Envelope`, `ReviewFinding`, and the `previous:` slot were never defined, although the story owns `src/phase-engine/envelopes/types.ts` and AC2, AC3 (`ReviewFinding.met === false`, 'a blocking item') and two DoD items are written directly against their shape. Declared both types in Contracts and recorded `previous?: Envelope` on DF1.1's `PhaseParams` in both stories.

Secrets-invariant defect: INV-2 asserted `redactSecrets` prevents a subprocess-printed provider key from reaching the envelope, but the cited function (`cli-anything/src/redact.ts:62`) is parent-env-value-derived, not pattern-based — it masks only values >=8 chars held under a `SECRET_KEY_RE`-matching env name — and the story omitted its second `parentEnv` argument entirely. The DoD redaction test as written would not have passed. INV-2 now states the real contract and requires the adapter be handed the spawn env; the test seeds `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and asserts the `[REDACTED:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]` marker.

The subprocess-result type was named `QualityResult` in the Overview, E2E slice, and adapter-invariant note but `QualityCheckResult` in the Contracts block the story owns. Unified to `QualityCheckResult`.

The new `GateReport` collides by name with the already-exported `GateReport`/`GateReportSchema` in P0.11's gate chassis at `src/gate/gate-runner.ts:117`, which has a different shape (`overall: PASS|FAIL`, `assertions`). Recorded as a deliberately distinct type at `src/phase-engine/gates/report.ts`, with the chassis explicitly untouched.

`gate_fail` was described as 'persisted' while the trigger surface defers gate-evidence rows in the SQLite trace store to DF1.4, leaving no persistence target at this story. Observability Contract now routes gate events through DF1.1's file-backed `PhaseJournal` port, with `gate_results` rows named as DF1.4's.
Dependency edges listed P0.5 unqualified; R5 §6 fact 18 records it as `in-review`, not done (issue #51 / PR #98). Qualified in place, noting this story needs only the script's exit code.

surviving.summary: The `PhaseJournal` port has no declared method signatures or record shape, though DF1.4 swaps the SQLite trace store in behind it and DF1.2 now persists gate events through it. The explicit Deviation/assumption note bounds the risk ('DF1.4 widens the port; it does not fork the lifecycle'), so a dev is not blocked, but there is no interface to code DF1.4's adapter against until DF1.1 lands.

`asEnvelope(result, label)` takes a `label` while `QualityCheckResult` already carries a `name`; the story never says which populates the envelope's label or what happens when they disagree. Inferable (the explicit `label` wins, per `MOD/quality.py:193-211`) but unstated.

INV-4's credential-shaped rejection lists field names (`key`/`token`/`secret`/`password`) that a `.strict()` closed schema already rejects as unknown fields per AC2; only the value-shape half (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `Bearer `, `-----BEGIN`) adds enforcement.
